title: Desire to serve is the first qualification for the work
setting: Joseph Smith Sr. visited his son at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in early 1829. Joseph had apparently not translated the plates since the lost manuscript of June 1828. He dictated this revelation for his father shortly before translation began again. A scribe later corrected the date in Revelation Book 1 from 1828 to 1829.
summary: The revelation announces that a marvelous work is about to come forth. It tells those who enter God’s service to serve with heart, might, mind, and strength. Then it says that desire to serve is itself a call to the work. It compares the moment to a field ready for harvest. The worker who reaps with energy also gains salvation. It lists faith, hope, charity, and love as the qualities that fit a person for the work. It ends with a list of ten virtues and the promise to ask and receive.

contextNote.title: A call that begins with wanting to serve
contextNote.text: Joseph Smith Sr. held no office when this revelation came. Verse 3 makes desire the starting point: if you want to serve, you are called. Verse 2 then sets the standard for that service: all heart, might, mind, and strength. Verse 4 explains the urgency with a harvest image. A ripe field will not wait for a better season. Verse 5 names what qualifies the worker, and none of it is rank or training. In this text, a call is first a willingness that God then shapes.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 treats this revelation as a call to anyone willing to serve. Which of the qualities in verses 5–6 could you develop this week, and how?
reviewNote: Read all 7 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, February 1829, to Joseph Smith Sr. JSP historical introduction read for the date change, the January 1829 visit, and translation resuming. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting now says Joseph had “apparently” not translated since June 1828 and that one scribe corrected the 1828 date, per JSP.
